acceptance: `make -C go apicover-enforce` passes on a quiet host three runs in a row (red today, intermittently)
The real-tmux fixtures' boot budget is derived, not a fixed wall-clock constant

consumed.resolution: Same root cause as realtmux-tests-interfere-across-concurrent-test-processes (consumed in the same change). The package-parallel apicover run was slow not from raw load but because the run itself links and executes hundreds of new test binaries, which queue macOS's first-run scan (XprotectService) of the fake-CLI scripts the real-tmux fixtures wrote and ran directly (10-22 s per first run under a concurrent floor); a shared, stale evolve-bridge server running the operator's login shell added 0.5-3 s. Every fake is now installed with internal/fakeclitest (a hard link to the already-scanned test binary that runs the script through its interpreter) and internal/tmuxtest.Main gives each test process its own evolve-bridge-t<pid> server with /bin/sh panes, so the fixed boot budget holds; deriving the budget was unnecessary once the boot path stopped queueing. einject's fixed 8 s sender now lives as long as the run. Incident: docs/incidents/2026-10-06-realtmux-tests-share-a-stale-tmux-server.md.

fix: Make the boot wait of the real-tmux fixtures load-aware (derive it from a measured boot of the fake REPL, or run these tests serially under a shared lock like the integration tier's retake), so a slow host yields a slow pass, never a false red; the local floor mirror must not go red where CI is green.
summary: On 2026-09-30 the local `make -C go apicover-enforce` (go test -count=1 -tags integration -coverprofile over every enforced package at once) failed twice on internal/bridge real-tmux tests: TestRealTmuxSandboxTerminalConfinement (train #731's floor), then TestRealTmuxSandboxTerminalConfinement, TestRealTmux_BracketedMultilinePromptPreservesBytes, TestRealTmux_E2E_LiveInjection_UnblocksAgent and TestRealTmux_HappyPath (PR #732's floor), each 'REPL prompt never appeared' then exit 80. Both times the package passed alone under the same invocation (42.7s), passed in the same floor's test-integration, and the diffs never touched internal/bridge; CI's go jobs were green. The first run overlapped another heavy suite on the host; the second ran alone, so the package-parallel coverage run itself supplies enough load. A third run on 2026-09-30 (PR #736's floor, 9b2f08d6) failed ten TestRealTmux_* tests in internal/bridge the same way ('REPL prompt never appeared after 60s', exit 80) while wave 47's own claude sessions ran; the package passed alone (APICOVER_PKGS=./internal/bridge: 124/124 exported covered), CI was green, and the diff never touched the bridge.
title: Real-tmux bridge tests fail under apicover-enforce's package-parallel run: the sandboxed fake REPL misses its boot budget (3 occurrences)
